title: When, Not How Much: Evaluating Time-Series Foundation Models on Sparse Events
abstract: arXiv:2609.39386v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Pretrained time-series foundation models (TSFMs) are evaluated as forecasters of future values, yet for sparse series many decisions depend only on which future periods contain activity. Standard benchmarks do not assess this. On five sparse datasets, we rank positions within forecast windows that contain both events and zeros. The released point forecasts of 12 TSFMs improve chance-corrected average precision over training-free references by at most 0.031, and in chance-corrected AUC the median TSFM falls below them on every dataset. With event supervision, linear probes of six frozen backbones improve on their backbone's point forecast in 29 of 30 backbone--dataset pairs. Averaging the predicted quantiles instead of taking their median improves the ranking of most TSFMs that forecast the median, and on two datasets the strongest such outputs rival the probes. translated_title: 何时，而非多少：在稀疏事件上评估时间序列基础模型
translated_abstract: 预训练时间序列基础模型（TSFM）通常被评估为未来数值的预测器，然而对于稀疏序列，许多决策仅取决于未来哪些时段包含活动，而标准基准并未对此进行评估。在五个稀疏数据集上，作者对预测窗口内同时包含事件和零值的位置进行排序。结果显示：12个已发布TSFM的点预测在机会校正平均精度上相比免训练参考基线最多仅提升0.031，且在机会校正AUC上，中位数TSFM在所有数据集上均低于这些基线。在事件监督下，六个冻结骨干网络的线性探针在30个骨干-数据集组合中有29个优于其骨干自身的点预测。对预测分位数取平均而非取中位数，可改善大多数预测中位数的TSFM的排名，并且在两个数据集上，此类最强输出可媲美探针。探针相对于原始上下文学习者的优势取决于具体数据集。
tldr: 该研究提出用“预测未来哪些时段包含稀疏事件”的排序任务而非数值预测来评估时间序列基础模型，发现其点预测几乎不超过简单基线，而对冻结骨干网络训练线性探针在绝大多数情况下显著更优。
en_tdlr: This paper reframes time-series foundation model evaluation as ranking which future periods contain sparse events rather than forecasting values, showing their point forecasts barely beat training-free baselines while linear probes on frozen backbones win in 29 of 30 backbone-dataset pairs.
